text:
sophia: Heads-up — saw a cluster of nodes in apne3 stuck in early boot after the latest BMC push. GPUs on those racks are not reporting and provisioning is failing. ~10 nodes, ~80 GPUs impacted, ~3% capacity hit. @ajay can you triage? :eyes:
ajay: On it. Any logs or IPMI output? Suspect keystore replay causing the BMC to restart into recovery mode if it sees the same key ID twice.
sophia: Pasting the short syslog snippet from out-of-band collector:
```
Apr 20 03:12:44 bmc[pid=1423] keystore: replay detected id=0x3a7f
Apr 20 03:12:44 bmc[pid=1423] watchdog: trigger cold-reboot
Apr 20 03:12:46 kernel: early boot: invalid signature, entering recovery
Apr 20 03:12:47 provisioning: node-apse3-rack7-n12 failed to update status: not-provisionable
```
kevin: Are these nodes part of the staged keystore rollout? I thought we were doing staggered windows yesterday.
sophia: They were in the second wave — rollout window 02:00-04:00. We saw a replay spike exactly at 03:12. ops-bot alerted the provisioning queue.
ops-bot: [alert] provisioning-queue-apne3 latency > 95th percentile, backlog 42 requests.
ajay: Reproduced locally on a test BMC image — when the keystore index resets during async writes, the BMC treats it as a replay and moves to recovery. Need a short mitigation: stop further keystore pushes, rotate to new key IDs, and perform a targeted manual recon on affected racks.
maria: Can we hotfix the keystore publisher to use monotonic counters instead of resetting per-bmc? That'd avoid replay semantics.
ajay: Agreed long-term. Short-term plan I propose:
1) Pause keystore rollout immediately (CI job id: ks-roll-2026-17)
2) Run manual rekey on impacted hosts with new key ID namespace
3) Drain and reprovision affected racks: run `redwood-provisioner drain --rack=apne3-rack7 --reason="bmc-keystore-replay"` then `ipmitool chassis power cycle` if they don't self-unstick
4) Canary 3 nodes in apne3-rack9 before resuming any pushes
5) Postmortem and rollback the publisher change if needed.
kevin: For step 3, add a rate limit so we don't cause a mass coldboot cascade across the region. Suggest `--parallel=2` for the drain tool. Also notify CS about potential capacity impact.
sophia: I already opened a quick note to CS and customers in apne region: https://go/ops/apne3-keystore (link) — kept it minimal.
maria: Ops budget note — if we end up re-provisioning 10 nodes that's ~80 GPU-hours plus manual ops time. Flagging for finance to track.
ajay: Doing the manual rekey now on a single node to validate. I'll paste the ipmitool sequence once verified.
(15m later)
ajay: Verified: rekey with new ID avoids replay. ipmitool sequence used:
```
# set new key namespace
ipmitool raw 0x30 0x70 0x00 0x03 0x01 0x00
# trigger bmc reload
ipmitool mc reset cold
```
sophia: Good. I'll start drains on rack7 with `--parallel=2` and tag runs with `keystore-replay-mitigation`.
kevin: Keep an eye on provisioning backlog and GPU scheduler. If backlog > 100, we should flip routing to eu fallback for non-latency-sensitive jobs.
ops-bot: [update] provisioning-queue-apne3 backlog reduced to 12 after two drains.
maria: Please add a ticket for the publisher fix (monotonic counters) and include rollout gating: require 24h canary with telemetry watch.
ajay: Created ticket INFRA-8492 and assigned to eng-infra/reliability. I'll start a canary tomorrow 01:00 UTC.
sophia: Thanks team — keeping this thread for the remediation notes. Will update if we hit regressions. :thumbsup:
